articles.title: Sleeping beside daughter, Delhi govt employee stabbed multiple times: How wife, her gym trainer lover  plotted attack
articles.summary: GHAZIABAD: Shashank Kanthariya thought his wife was leaving home every morning to go to the gym.
articles.body: GHAZIABAD: Shashank Kanthariya thought his wife was leaving home every morning to go to the gym. But police suspect that the routine became part of a conspiracy to kill him after he discovered her alleged affair with her gym trainer and decided to move out of the city.On Monday morning, while the 35-year-old Delhi government employee was asleep beside his young daughter at their home in Vasundhara, the trainer allegedly entered the house through an unlocked door and stabbed him repeatedly.Kanthariya, a senior accountant with the Delhi government, was taken to a nearby hospital after the attack and is currently admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU). His daughter, who was sleeping beside him, woke up during the assault and began crying, alerting neighbours. The child escaped without injuries.Police arrested Kanthariya's wife, Priya (32), and her suspected lover, Pratap Singh (30), a gym trainer, on Tuesday. Both were produced before a court and sent to judicial custody.Affair came to light in SeptemberAccording to ACP (Indirapuram) Suryabali Maurya, Singh began working at the gym Priya frequented in Vasundhara in January this year. He became her trainer, and the two allegedly entered into a relationship the following month.The relationship continued until Kanthariya learnt about the alleged affair towards the end of September. He confronted Priya and asked her to end the relationship. He also told her to either change gyms or stop attending the one where Singh worked.Police suspect that the dispute escalated when Kanthariya decided to move out of their home and began looking for a house in Delhi. Priya allegedly opposed the plan, while Kanthariya intended to finalise a property on Sunday.Investigators suspect that Priya informed Singh about her husband's plans and that the two subsequently conspired to kill him.Wife allegedly left door unlockedPolice said Priya routinely left home around 5am to visit the gym, leaving the front door unlocked while her husband and daughter were asleep. On Monday morning, she allegedly followed the same routine, giving Singh an opportunity to enter the house.Singh allegedly arrived armed with two knives and attacked Kanthariya while he was sleeping. The victim woke up during the assault and raised an alarm, while his daughter began crying. The noise alerted neighbours, who rushed to the house as the attacker fled.ACP Maurya said Singh took advantage of Priya's departure to enter the flat and attack her husband. Police suspect the attack was part of the plan the two had allegedly worked out.Society guards chased accusedAfter fleeing the house, Singh was spotted by a resident of the society, MT Joshi, who noticed blood on his hands and attempted to catch him. Singh allegedly pushed Joshi aside and continued running, managing to get past the security guards.The guards then chased him on a motorcycle, caught him and handed him over to police. Two knives were recovered from his possession, police said.Meanwhile, neighbours rushed the injured Kanthariya to a nearby hospital. He remains in the ICU, while his daughter was unharmed.Brother's complaint leads to FIRKanthariya's brother, Ritesh, filed a police complaint following the attack. An FIR was subsequently registered against Priya and Singh under sections 109 (attempt to murder), 333 (house trespass after preparation for hurt, assault or wrongful restraint) and 61(2) (criminal conspiracy) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).Police arrested both accused on Tuesday and produced them before a court, which remanded them to judicial custody.Kanthariya and Priya married in 2021 and have a young daughter. articles.title: Uber cabbie arrested for physically restraining, threatening Gurgaon techie over fare dispute; how ordeal unfolded
articles.summary: Uber driver Yasir arrested in Gurgaon after woman alleged threats, restraint and being followed home over fare dispute; police say account used fake name Jamil Jahid Khan.
articles.body: GURGAON: The Uber driver, who allegedly threatened a woman, physically restrained her and followed her to her home over a fare dispute, was arrested on Wednesday after police took suo motu cognizance of her social media post.“Teams from Palam Vihar police station and the Sector 39 crime branch used technical assistance to identify the accused — Yasir (26) from Nuh’s Ghasera village — and gather information about him before arresting him,” police spokesperson Sandeep Turan said. TOIhad reported the incident on Wednesday.Police said preliminary investigation revealed that Yasir had created his Uber account using the name Jamil Jahid Khan, the name mentioned by the woman in her post on X. The woman, a software engineer and artificial intelligence professional, had posted that the driver demanded Rs 1,479 against the fare of around Rs 625 displayed on her Uber app for a ride from Delhi airport to the city. She alleged that when she refused to pay the higher amount, the driver misbehaved with her and threatened to kill her. The incident sparked concern on social media, with users urging the police to take action and calling for stronger measures to protect passengers.According to the police, the matter came to their notice during social media monitoring. Police attempted to contact the woman through X before taking suo motu cognizance and registering an FIR on the basis of her post. In her account of the incident, the woman said the confrontation took place around 4.45am after she booked the Uber cab from Delhi airport for what she described as a 20-minute ride. The app showed a fare of approximately Rs 625, but the driver allegedly demanded Rs 1,479 after showing her a screenshot of a fare quote from Rapido.She said she paid the fare displayed on the Uber app, following which the driver allegedly locked the car and refused to let her retrieve her luggage unless she paid the higher amount. She alleged that he held her arm, followed her to her residence, forced the gate and threatened her life. The woman also raised concerns over her inability to access Uber’s safety support option while trying to report the incident. She later said Uber had contacted her and confirmed that the driver had been barred from the platform.“We were committed to ensuring women’s safety and that strict legal action would be taken against anyone found involved in acts that threaten or compromise women’s safety,” Turan added.The provisions, under which the accused has been arrested, relate to assault or use of criminal force against a woman with the intent to outrage her modesty (Section 74), words, gestures or acts intended to insult the modesty of a woman (Section 79), punishment for wrongful restraint (Section 126(2)), wrongful confinement (Section 127), punishment for assault or criminal force otherwise than on grave provocation (Section 131), criminal intimidation (Section 351(2)) and the right of private defence of body and property (Section 35) of BNS.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Gurgaon | Silver Rate in Gurgaon | Bank Holidays in Gurgaon | Public Holidays in Gurgaon | Gurgaon AQI | Weather in Gurgaon | Petrol Price in Gurgaon | Diesel Price in Gurgaon | CNG Price in Gurgaon | LPG Price in GurgaonStay updated with the latest Gurgaon news. articles.title: Twin towers again: Allahabad HC orders demolition of Ghaziabad’s Gulmohar Greens buildings, FIR against builder
articles.summary: Allahabad HC orders demolition of Gulmohar Greens twin towers in Ghaziabad, FIR against builder, action on GDA officials over illegal extra floors and units.
articles.body: GHAZIABAD: Allahabad high court has ordered the demolition of two 10-storey towers at Gulmohar Greens society in Mohan Nagar, ruling they were built illegally, and ordered an FIR against Friends Land Developers, the company that built it.In a ruling with echoes of the Supertech Emerald Court case, which paved the way for demolition of two residential skyscrapers at the Noida society in 2022, the high court chastised Ghaziabad Development Authority (GDA) for colluding with the builder in allowing the two towers at Gulmohar Greens to take shape illegally. A division bench of justices Sudhanshu Chauhan and Saral Srivastava also ordered demolition of two extra floors built in four other towers, 16 to 19, within two months. The extra floors took these towers to 10 storeys from the originally sanctioned eight. There are a total of 32 flats (all under construction) across the illegal floors of these four towers.Towers 27 and 28, which are to be fully razed, have 80 unoccupied flats. The court directed the Ghaziabad administration and police to provide security and assistance to GDA during the demolition, setting a time frame of two months to complete the exercise.The bench ordered the state govt to initiate disciplinary proceedings within a month against then GDA vice-chairperson Atul Vats, under whose watch the construction took place. GDA was directed to pay Rs 50,000 to each of the 11 petitioners in the case within two months. “The officers of GDA are also in collusion with the promoter, and because of their slipshod approach, the petitioners and residents of the society had to suffer a lot,” the court stated. Calling it dereliction of duty by Vats, the order said, “...despite having knowledge about said fact, the vice-chairperson has sanctioned the third compounding by order dated Dec 18, 2024”.Slapping a fine of Rs 25 lakh on Friends Land Developers, it ordered police to register the FIR within two weeks of the judgment. For illegal construction on common areas, it directed the builder to return the sale price of these areas to 85 ground-floor residents, along with construction cost and 10% interest. “It is a clear case where the promoter has misrepresented the correct facts and played fraud upon the apartment owners by selling common areas, and thus has committed an offence,” the court ruled.In its Aug 31, 2021, verdict on Supertech’s twin towers Apex and Ceyane in Noida’s Sector 93A, Supreme Court had pulled up Noida Authority, saying the case revealed “a nefarious complicity of the planning authority” in the developer’s violations. It had held that the illegal construction was achieved through collusion between Supertech’s management and Noida Authority officials. “The record of this case is replete with instances which highlight the collusion between the officers of Noida Authority with the appellant and its management,” the court had said.The 100-metre-tall towers were razed on Aug 28, 2022, using controlled implosion, generating 80,000 tonnes of debris and prompting stricter scrutiny of real estate projects across NCR.Gulmohar Greens RWA had moved the high court against illegal construction in 2025, alleging deviations from the original layout plan that had proposed 34 towers with 904 dwelling units. Residents alleged 112 units were added by the builder without their consent after paying a compounding fee to GDA thrice for approvals for layout deviations.In its 95-page judgment, the court noted that the project began in 2006 and remains incomplete more than 20 years later. It also observed that the builder chose not to obtain a completion certificate, although the UP Apartments Act, 2010, makes it its responsibility. “In such a situation, apartment owners cannot afford to wait till the time the promoter obtains a completion certificate. Because of this compulsion and constraints, apartment owners have no option but to occupy the apartments to ease out their financial burden,” the court said.The case dates to 2006, when the original promoter, SVP Builders India Limited, teamed up with Friends Land Developers and applied for a map sanction to develop Gulmohar Greens. The plan was for 904 units in 34 towers, each with a basement and eight storeys, on 87,930 sqm. The society is located near Hindon air base, and Indian Air Force officers objected that 4,560 sqm of the land belonged to the defence ministry.GDA cancelled the map approval on July 3, 2010, but the promoter had by then built 720 of the 904 sanctioned units. It applied for the first compounding on Nov 15, 2011, and GDA compounded the 720 existing units. The map also sanctioned 374 new units.“The promoter introduced modifications in the basement, machine room and ground floors of Towers 2 and 3. On Jan 13, 2015, it again applied for a second compounding, which too was sanctioned,” Group Captain VVS Rana (retd), a resident and one of the petitioners, told TOI. “The promoter again introduced deviation in the second compounding map and applied for third compounding on Dec 18, 2024. The promoter did not take consent of petitioners while applying for the compounding, which is in violation of Section 5 (3) (a) of the UP Apartment (Promotion of Construction, Ownership and Maintenance) Rules, and yet the map was sanctioned,” Rana said.The builder, according to petitioners, also encroached on common areas to create space for amenities like a machine room and generator room. In 2025, 11 residents filed a case in Allahabad HC. GDA vice-chairperson Nand Kishore Kalal said the authority was yet to go through the judgment. “The court’s order will be followed in letter and spirit,” he said.Friends Land Developers promoter Vijay Jindal could not be reached for a comment.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Noida | Silver Rate in Noida | Bank Holidays in Noida | Public Holidays in Noida | Noida AQI | Weather in Noida | Petrol Price in Noida | Diesel Price in Noida | CNG Price in Noida | LPG Price in NoidaStay updated with the latest Noida news. articles.title: In 2016, Megan Fox bought a $3.3 million Malibu home, then sued for $5 million over alleged mold and other defects; after a three-year court fight, she reportedly accepted a $100,000 settlement in 2021
articles.summary: For all its picturesque charm, a dream home can sometimes conceal a nightmare behind its colourful walls and landscaped gardens.
articles.body: For all its picturesque charm, a dream home can sometimes conceal a nightmare behind its colourful walls and landscaped gardens. Hollywood actress Megan Fox learned the hard way after buying a sprawling Malibu property that she later said was plagued by mold, water damage and other costly defects. What started out as a multimillion-dollar real estate purchase eventually became a three-year legal battle, highlighting the dangers of buying luxury property even when it appears idyllic on the surface.Controversial Malibu house of dreamsFox purchased the four-bedroom Malibu property for $3.3 million in May 2016 from Cynthia Pett-Dante, longtime manager for actor Brad Pitt, Fox News and the Daily Mail reported. The home was in the Ramirez Canyon area of the gated community and had about 3,300 square feet of living space on a two-acre estate.It wasn’t just the interiors that appealed. According to Realtor, the home had colorful finishes, unique wallpaper, decorative tiles, and a bohemian vibe. The grounds featured fruit trees, a greenhouse, stone walls, winding trails and small bridges. Outdoor amenities included a swimming pool, sports court and an in-ground trampoline.But the beautiful surroundings apparently masked serious problems. Fox later said the property had mold, leaks and water damage and estimated the cost of fixing the problems at more than $500,000.$5 million lawsuit, health claimsIn 2018, roughly two years after the purchase, Fox sued Pett-Dante and others associated with the transaction for $5 million. Fox News and the Daily Mail reported that the actress claims the condition of the property caused chronic migraines, stress and other health problems.The lawsuit also questioned water damage, problems with the septic tank and structures on the property that Fox claimed were not properly permitted. Another concern, according to court documents, was extensive landscaping and animal facilities allegedly built to house rescued animals.But the dispute was over conflicting accounts of what had been disclosed before the sale. Pett-Dante’s lawyers said Fox and her representatives were told about a number of defects before going ahead with the purchase, the Daily Mail reported. Court documents also revealed that Fox's real estate lawyer had expressed serious reservations about the transaction.In testimony, Fox admitted she hadn't read certain emails, inspection reports and disclosures herself, relying on professionals to review documents and advise her. She went ahead with the purchase, the reports said, as it was within her budget and would put her children into a school district she liked.Legal battle ends in settlementThe dispute ended in 2021 when Fox reportedly agreed to a $100,000 settlement offered by Pett-Dante under California’s settlement-offer provisions, according to the Daily Mail and Fox News. The amount was well short of the $5 million initially sought in damages.The settlement opened the door to dismiss the case with prejudice, ending the three-year legal battle. The court proceedings had also revealed the disagreement about the extent of the property’s defects and what the buyers knew before the sale.The house goes back on the marketBut the Malibu residence still drew real estate interest despite its legal history. The home was listed in April 2021 for $4.65 million and went into contingent sale status, the realtor said.The Daily Mail report adds that its return to the market has sparked fresh questions about the importance of property disclosures, particularly when a home has been linked to allegations of mold and water damage.Fox’s experience is a reminder that luxury real estate is more than simply location, architecture and beautiful scenery. Even for what appears to be the ideal Hollywood hideaway, comprehensive inspections, a close examination of disclosures and a solid knowledge of possible repair costs are critical.Images Courtesy: istock and WikipediaYou use AI every day. articles.title: Arab parties claim kingmaker status in Israel
articles.summary: Israel's Arab parties appear to secure a record number of seats in parliament and could emerge as kingmakers after strong turnout in Tuesday's election.
articles.body: Israel's Arab parties appear to secure a record number of seats in parliament and could emerge as kingmakers after strong turnout in Tuesday's election. Vote tallies show the two main Arab parties on course to win around 19 seats, nearly double their current representation in the Knesset. The two main parties are Yousef Jabareen-led Joint List and Ra'am, led by Mansour Abbas.Yousef Jabareen, the leader of the Arab-dominated Joint List, said his party would seek to use its projected 12 seats "to facilitate getting rid of Netanyahu's govt and hopefully helping to change the political situation in Israel". Jabareen said the Joint List could not join an Eisenkot-led govt because of its support for Israel's military campaign in Gaza and occupation of southern Lebanon. But he left open the possibility of bolstering Eisenkot's bloc from the outside, propping up a minority govt that could survive confidence votes. "We have our demands to protect our community, to advance the rights of our community and to promote equality for our community," said Jabareen, speaking from his home in the Arab town of Umm al-Fahm.The second main Arab party, Ra'am, is led by Mansour Abbas. He has sought to make Ra'am a more attractive coalition partner, adding a Jewish former police official to its slate and saying he would join an Eisenkot-led govt.Speaking to Israeli television after voting wrapped on Tuesday night, Ra'am chief Mansour Abbas said: "I believe we can overcome the difficulties ... and I think that most voters for the (Eisenkot) bloc do want to see (a) govt with the Ra'am party." He said senior members of Eisenkot's bloc had discussed a possible deal with him even before the election. "Everyone is talking to us, not just the change bloc. A few days ago, a very, very senior member of the right approached me."Eisenkot ruled out forming a govt with any of the Arab parties during the campaign, citing what he called a lack of shared values, including recognition of Israel as a Jewish and democratic state.Netanyahu's Likud party confirmed it would not negotiate with any Arab party to try to form a govt. "Not a chance," spokesman Guy Levy said at the party's headquarters in Jerusalem. "It's not even a question that should be asked."Who is Mansour Abbas?Mansour Abbas (52) is an Arab-Israeli politician, dentist and leader of Ra'am. Elected to Knesset in 2019, he reshaped Arab politics by advocating a pragmatic, domestic-focused approach. Instead of making engagement conditional on the wider Israeli-Palestinian conflict, he prioritises civil gains for Arab citizens, focusing on crime, socioeconomic inequality, infrastructure and municipal funding. He also briefly served in an Israeli ruling coalition from 2021 to 2022.What is Joint List?Joint List is an alliance of Arab-majority parties in Israel, formed in 2015 to unite the vote of Arab citizens. It includes Ahmed Tibi's Ta'al and has historically brought together secular, nationalist and left-leaning parties such as Hadash. It campaigns on civil equality, tackling crime in Arab communities and ending the occupation, and has backed govts from outside rather than joining them.How are Arabs placed in IsraelArab citizens of Israel, who often identify as Arab Israelis or Palestine citizens of Israel, comprise 20% of the population, or roughly 2.1 million people. They are central to the medical sector. Data from Israeli ministry of health and Taub Center for Social Policy Studies in Israel show Arabs account for over 20% of physicians, nearly a quarter of nurses and almost half of licensed pharmacists. Two Arab citizens have served as Supreme Court judges, while Arab engineers, scholars, writers and athletes, have visible public roles.Arab parties' past supportFor decades, Arab parties provided outside support to governments. Cabinet representation was limited to individual appointments, including Druze lawmaker Salah Tarif in 2001, Labor's Raleb Majadele in 2007, and later Issawi Frej and Ayoob Kara. A significant change came in 2021 when Abbas's Islamist Ra'am joined Naftali Bennett-Yair Lapid's ruling coalition.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Amazon layoffs hit devices and ‌services unit; company's 'early morning' email to laid off employees says: A thorough review of ​our ...
articles.summary: Amazon layoffs are back. Ecommerce giant has announced new job cuts.
articles.body: Amazon layoffs are back. Ecommerce giant has announced new job cuts. According to a report in Reuters, Amazon is cutting about 250 jobs in its devices and ‌services unit after weeks of product rollouts including new Kindle e-readers and tablet computers. The company reportedly confirmed the job cuts after a Reuters inquiry. "We've made the difficult decision to eliminate a small number ⁠of roles," a spokesperson said. The layoffs will help the company "operate more efficiently and better align with our product roadmap," the statement added.According to the report, quoting a person familiar with the matter, the ​layoffs impact no more than 250 jobs, and are primarily in software development teams. As is the company's custom, text messages and emails were sent to employees early Wednesday morning (October 28). A layoff email, reportedly seen by ​Reuters, was ​from Cherie ⁠Robinson, a human resources vice president in devices and services, saying ​that the company had undergone "a thorough review of ​our ⁠structure" resulting in the need for cuts.In January this year, Amazon announced that it is cutting 16,000 jobs across the company. This announcement came after the e-commerce company laid off 14,000 people in October. During January layoffs, senior VP of People Experience and Technology Beth Galetti told employees that these layoffs were made for “reducing layers, increasing ownership, and removing bureaucracy.” She noted that the reason for the second round of massive layoffs within three months was that several teams in the company hadn’t finished their restructuring. “Some of you might ask if this is the beginning of a new rhythm – where we announce broad reductions every few months. That’s not our plan. But just as we always have, every team will continue to evaluate the ownership, speed, and capacity to invent for customers, and make adjustments as appropriate,” she said.Amazon unveils new lineup of Alexa devicesIncidentally, the job cuts in the devices division came on the day Amazon unveiled five new Alexa-powered devices including a redesigned Echo Show 16 smart display and a photo frame with ‌built-in Alexa. The new product launches come as Amazon pushes its latest version of the voice assistant into customers' homes. Amazon is rolling out the devices as it ⁠faces growing competition from rivals including Apple, as well as AI companies such as OpenAI that have hardware ambitions.The Echo Show 16, which has a ​16-inch screen, built-in Fire TV and Amazon's ⁠first Echo Show camera with night vision, ​is priced at $499.99. A new Echo Studio ​speaker with a built-in camera, which lets Alexa recognize objects held up to it and lets users check ​on a room remotely, is priced at $249.99. The new Echo ​Dot is priced at $99.99. The device includes a built-in smart home hub and ‌Wi-Fi ⁠extender for the first time.Echo Time is a bedside clock, priced at $199. According to the company, it uses sleep-sensing technology to wake users during lighter sleep, without a wearable device. The Alexa ​Photo Frame, ​starting at $199.99, ⁠syncs pictures automatically from Amazon Photos.Amazon's open memo to engineersJust a day earlier, Amazon published a memo it shared with engineers in September on its website. Titled: 'Update from Amazon engineering leadership on the role of the developer in the age of AI'; the memo has Amazon engineering leaders revise the role guideline for software development engineers, underscoring what matters most is the outcome, not which tools are used. "We all need to embrace this change and take the time to learn, or we risk being left behind. We’re just seeing the beginning of AI’s effect on software engineering. While we have a vision for what the future looks like, there’s a lot that’s still emerging. We are certain that whatever future best practices are, AI will be at the center of software engineering practice," reads the memo.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Woman tries to hurl purse at Bombay high court judge after eviction order goes against her
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Bombay high court came down heavily on a litigant who tried to throw her purse at a judge after an order was passed against her and her three
articles.body: MUMBAI: Bombay high court came down heavily on a litigant who tried to throw her purse at a judge after an order was passed against her and her three children.“Minder Gurmit Singh Thukral has behaved in a wholly inappropriate manner, which also amounts to contempt of court,” justice Madhav Jamdar noted in Tuesday’s order.HC was hearing a contempt petition against the Thukrals. An eviction decree in a 2009 suit filed by the landlord against Thukral’s father-in-law was executed in April 2025. Thereafter the Thukrals re-entered the property. The landlord’s family moved HC.Justice Jamdar said, “prima facie, I am satisfied that the conduct of the respondents amounts to interference in the administration of justice.”He appointed the court receiver to take symbolic possession of the premises by Wednesday and remain present on Thursday for handover of possession to the petitioners.Further, if possession is not handed over, the court receiver shall take physical possession and immediately hand it over to the landlord. HC permitted taking police protection.It was then that Thukral started crying and shouting. She tried to throw her purse at the judge but stopped herself. She submitted a written apology.But Justice Jamdar questioned her conduct, saying, “just because an order is passed against you, doesn’t mean you will behave in such a manner.”He summoned the police, who removed Thukral from the courtroom. Justice Jamdar indicated imposing heavy costs and initiating contempt proceedings against her. articles.title: Red signal, system failure, fatal impact: How Spain’s train collision unfolded
articles.summary: Spain is investigating a deadly high-speed train collision in the central province of Toledo after a state-owned RENFE train struck the rear of an IRYO
articles.body: Spain is investigating a deadly high-speed train collision in the central province of Toledo after a state-owned RENFE train struck the rear of an IRYO train that had stopped on the tracks, derailing carriages and killing at least 68 people.The crash occurred at approximately 8:54 am local time (0754 GMT), roughly 120 km south of Madrid. It follows a January collision in Córdoba province that killed more than 40 people and a separate accident near Barcelona in which a train driver was killed.The regional government of Castilla-La Mancha said 58 people were receiving medical treatment in hospitals. Rescue teams searched the wreckage for survivors and bodies as emergency services worked to evacuate passengers from the most severely damaged coaches.According to Spain’s rail infrastructure operator ADIF, both trains were travelling south from Madrid towards Seville when the collision occurred on Wednesday morning. The RENFE train hit the stationary IRYO train, knocking two carriages of the latter off the tracks and derailing the front of the former.What caused the crash?The cause of the collision remains unknown. Esther Padilla, spokesperson for the Castilla-La Mancha regional government, said authorities had not yet established what led to the accident.Meanwhile, while addressing reporters in Madrid, Spain’s transport minister Óscar Puente said a computer communications failure disrupted the railway safety system, automatically stopping trains along a 63-kilometre (40-mile) stretch of track. The failure was followed by a decision to allow a southbound RENFE high-speed train to proceed despite a red signal, breaking the protocol, he said.According to CNN, the state-owned railway infrastructure manager ADIF took manual control of the system after the failure. Puente said the RENFE train was authorised to continue despite the signal prohibiting movement, with the decision reportedly made under erroneous instructions from a train controller. The train resumed travelling at about 124 miles per hour before colliding with a stationary IRYO train.“There was a red signal prohibiting movement, yet the train was authorized to proceed,” Puente said at a press conference on Wednesday. “It is a decision made under inexplicable circumstances.”Following the minister’s remarks, the Spanish trade union CSIF called for restraint while the investigation continued and urged the government to respect due process.“We demand that the Government respect the investigation and the presumption of innocence for the head of traffic at ADIF,” the union said.Investigators are expected to examine the communications failure, the decision to override the automatic stop and the authorisation that allowed the RENFE train to continue despite the red signal.The crash occurred on a stretch of railway between the towns of Urda and Los Yébenes, in an area surrounded by olive fields. The impact tore apart carriages and scattered debris down a gravel slope.Passenger Ignacio Relaño, who was travelling on the RENFE train, told Spanish state broadcaster TVE that the train had briefly stopped before moving again and colliding with the IRYO service.“We all felt the train abruptly slowing down and then the impact,” Relaño said. “The car leaned to one side like it was about to tip over. I hit my nose, everything went flying, luggage, cell phones. Everything shook.”A second deadly collision in a yearThe disaster has renewed scrutiny of Spain’s high-speed rail network, which had recorded no fatal accident on its dedicated high-speed lines since the network opened in 1992, according to AP.In January, 46 people died when an IRYO train derailed in southern Spain and struck an oncoming RENFE train. Prime minister Pedro Sánchez visited the latest crash site and announced three days of national mourning.“Today all of Spain is grieving,” prime minister Pedro Sánchez said, as he announced three days of national mourning following the deadly collision. “It is unacceptable for a country like Spain to suffer two high-speed rail accidents in the same year,” he added. Authorities said 397 passengers were aboard the RENFE train and 147 on the IRYO service when the two trains collided.The disaster has renewed scrutiny of Spain’s high-speed rail network, which has expanded significantly over the past three decades. articles.body: US President Donald Trump has described Brazil’s presidential election as “very strange” after Brazilian senator Flávio Bolsonaro declared himself the country’s “true president-elect”, alleged electoral fraud and vowed to lead the opposition from the United States.Asked about Flávio’s claim, Trump said, “I'm not going to make a comment about that...I won't get involved. It was a very strange election, that's for sure.”Flávio, son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, arrived in the US with his family after leaving Brazil. He has said he would continue his political activities from abroad, alleging that he faced political persecution and that Brazil’s political system was becoming increasingly authoritarian.In a lengthy statement addressed to Brazilians and the international community on Wednesday, Flávio rejected suggestions that he had fled the country to escape scrutiny.“I want to make this clear: I did not flee Brazil; I left for Brazil’s sake,” he wrote, arguing that remaining in the country would have prevented him from exercising political leadership.Flávio alleges electoral fraud, challenges Lula’s victoryFlávio alleged that the October 25 presidential election was rigged in favour of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, claiming that Lula gained more than 10 million votes between the first and second rounds in what he described as a “mathematical impossibility”.He also questioned the extension of voting hours at some locations, accused judicial authorities of exceeding their jurisdiction and argued that alleged campaign violations warranted the annulment of the Lula-Alckmin ticket.The senator claimed that those responsible for what he called a stolen election belonged to a criminal organisation that had established a “tyranny” in Brazil.However, his statement did not provide evidence to establish that electoral fraud had occurred. Brazil’s Liberal Party (PL), which backed his candidacy, had earlier acknowledged the official election result while calling for concerns raised by the campaign to be addressed through political and democratic debate.Vows to lead opposition from USFlávio accused Brazil’s Supreme Federal Court of orchestrating political persecution against him and his father, Jair Bolsonaro. He alleged that judicial action against him could escalate from passport seizure to electronic monitoring, censorship, house arrest and eventual political conviction.He maintained that no arrest warrant had been issued against him and denied committing any crime.The senator said he had brought his family to the US to protect them and would continue his political activities from there. Drawing comparisons with figures such as French wartime leader Charles de Gaulle and Venezuelan opposition leaders, he portrayed his departure as part of a broader struggle for democracy.Addressing lawmakers and governors allied with him, Flávio said he would lead the opposition from the US and speak for supporters who, he claimed, could not freely express themselves in Brazil.He also named senator Rogério Marinho as his candidate for the presidency of the Senate and said he would soon outline a strategy to mobilise the opposition through what he described as peaceful and legitimate means.Flávio’s declaration marks a further escalation in his challenge to Lula’s victory. He had previously called for the election to be annulled, while the PL subsequently acknowledged the result proclaimed by Brazil’s Superior Electoral Court.You use AI every day. articles.title: A Texas artist began drawing portraits on rice using food colouring; her fleeting creations attracted millions of viewers and helped her build a million-subscriber channel
articles.summary: A Texas artist has transformed an everyday kitchen staple into a strange form of portraiture.
articles.body: A Texas artist has transformed an everyday kitchen staple into a strange form of portraiture. She creates intricate images from colored rice which last only a fraction of a second. Fried Rice Art artist Alissa Teo arranges individual grains into recognizable faces and designs before throwing them into the air and shooting the moment on camera. Her work has reached millions of viewers on the web and turned a tiny creative experiment into a successful business. What began as a family activity in 2021 has since grown into a popular social media channel and a source of commercial commissions.Rice portraits helped a Texas artist attracting millions of viewersAccording to KERA News, the Flower Mound artist developed her distinctive technique after spending more time at home with her family. Her background as a registered occupational therapist also influenced the idea, as rice had previously been a useful material for sensory activities with children.Teo began colouring rice and playing with it alongside her children during a period when her middle child was experiencing health complications. The activity offered a simple way for the family to spend time together while giving her an opportunity to return to her interest in art.As explained on the official Fried Rice Art website, Teo had enjoyed making art since childhood and had sold her work to classmates as a young artist. She later became an occupational therapist before changing her working arrangements to accommodate her family's needs.The rice creations eventually developed into something more ambitious. Her sister encouraged Teo to put her artwork on TikTok and she began posting her experiments online.Her early videos were garnering millions of views in days, the response much more than she had anticipated.The painstaking process behind each fleeting creationDespite their playful appearance, Teo's portraits require considerable preparation and precision. A report by Flower Mound Times described how she creates the images in a corner of her backyard, using a mobile phone and a tripod to record the final toss.Before the camera starts rolling, she carefully arranges coloured grains of rice to form a recognisable image. Tweezers and rulers help her place the tiny pieces and a tracing of the intended design helps with placement of the different colors.Her work table is covered with many bottles of colored dye so that she can build portraits with different shades and fine details. The process demands patience because even a small mistake can affect the appearance of the finished image.When Teo’s done arranging the rice he tosses it in the air. The grains briefly take on the desired image and then disperse and fall apart.The camera takes that instant of change so that the spectator can see the construction and the deconstruction of the work at the same time.The appeal lies in the brief existence of each portrait. Teo does not paint a finished image on canvas or paper, but rather an image that is to exist for an instant.The video recording is the permanent record of the artwork and allows viewers to see a process they may never otherwise see.A social media following that grew into a businessThe popularity of Fried Rice Art has helped Teo establish a substantial online presence. According to her official website, she has attracted more than 3.5 million followers on TikTok and 2.1 million subscribers on YouTube.Her audience has opened opportunities beyond social media views. The official Fried Rice Art portfolio lists collaborations with well-known companies and entertainment brands, including Disney, LEGO, Crayola, ESPN, Paramount, Puma and the Houston Texans.These projects have allowed Teo to apply her unusual technique to commercial campaigns and familiar characters. Flower Mound Times reported that she created an image of Tow Mater from the Disney film Cars as part of a project connected with the film's world.The commissions demonstrate how an unconventional artistic idea can find an audience beyond its original setting. Instead of relying on traditional materials, Teo uses coloured rice to create images that work particularly well in short videos, where viewers can see the arrangement, the toss and the moment of transformation.How does the artist put leftover rice to useAlthough the final toss scatters the carefully arranged grains, the rice does not necessarily go to waste. Teo's official website includes a dedicated section explaining how she reuses the material to make sensory bins for children.According to the website's sensory-bin guide, she catches much of the rice on a board beneath the artwork before collecting it and placing it in containers. She then adds age-appropriate toys and tools, such as tweezers, scoops, spoons and cups, to create activities for children.The containers can be adapted around different themes, including glow-in-the-dark designs. The tools also offer opportunities for children to practise coordination and fine motor skills by picking up, moving and sorting objects.This aspect of the business connects directly with Teo's earlier occupational therapy career. The same material that helps her create portraits for an online audience can also support hands-on activities for children.An artistic idea built around making people smileTeo's work has continued to cover a wide range of subjects, from recognisable characters and sports-related designs to flags, food, holidays and special occasions. Her official website says she has created more than 500 rice toss-ups for fans and companies combined.The variety allows her to respond to different audiences. Fried Rice Art describes the motivation behind the work as creating encouraging pieces that put a smile on people's faces. That approach also helps explain why the videos appeal to viewers who may have little interest in traditional art.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Hegseth fires top Pentagon military planner as Trump weighs fresh Iran strikes: Report
articles.summary: The Pentagon's senior officer responsible for military strategy and planning has been removed from his post as the Trump administration weighs its next
articles.body: The Pentagon's senior officer responsible for military strategy and planning has been removed from his post as the Trump administration weighs its next move in the war with Iran, adding to questions over leadership changes at the US Defence Department at a critical moment for regional security.Army Lt Gen Brett Sylvia's departure was confirmed by a US defence official on Wednesday, reported Associated Press. Sylvia headed the strategy, plans and policy directorate, known within the military as the J5, which helps coordinate military planning with the chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff and the president.The official, who spoke on condition of anonymity because the matter involved sensitive personnel issues, said no reason had been provided for Sylvia's removal and no immediate successor had been identified.The timing is significant as President Donald Trump is reportedly considering whether to resume attacks on Iran after the November 3 US midterm elections. Washington has alerted regional partners to prepare for possible renewed military action and the risk of Iranian retaliation, according to two diplomats briefed on the warnings.Trump has not taken a final decision on further strikes. However, the warnings have prompted concerns among regional governments about attacks on energy installations and other critical infrastructure if hostilities intensify.The J5 plays a central role in translating military objectives into operational plans. The Pentagon recently sent the USS Theodore Roosevelt aircraft carrier and amphibious ships carrying Marines towards the Persian Gulf, a deployment involving about 9,000 troops. The additional forces could help expand US military options, although their presence does not establish whether or when Trump will authorise another attack.Although regional governments are said to be preparing for the possibility that a renewed US campaign could trigger retaliation extending beyond the initial period of American strikes. The diplomats said US officials had indicated that a fresh round of military action could last several days, while Iranian counterattacks and actions by allied groups could prolong the confrontation.Iran, meanwhile, has continued to signal an interest in negotiations. Foreign minister Abbas Araghchi said Wednesday that Tehran “continues to give diplomacy a chance to succeed” and is working with mediators to review proposals it wants to use as a basis for restoring a ceasefire. Trump had previously rejected the proposal.The United Arab Emirates also urged the parties to avoid escalation, calling on them to “exercise wisdom and pursue political solutions to help contain tensions”.Trump keeps military option openTrump has alternated between suggesting the conflict could end soon and warning that further bombing remains possible. During a campaign appearance in Texas earlier this week, he said an end to the war could come “in a couple of weeks, if you don’t mind”. “Somebody asked me before, when will the war in Iran end?” Trump said. “I said, ‘Whenever I want it to end.’ It’ll be very quick, but we have to have it end properly, with total and complete -- a total statement, they will never have a nuclear weapon.”The conflict has also created political and economic pressures for the administration ahead of the midterms. Higher gasoline prices have weighed on voters, while the Pentagon's latest estimate puts the cost of the war to American taxpayers at $47.1 billion.Jonathan Schanzer, executive director of the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, warned that Tehran might not wait for Washington's preferred timeline if it believed an attack was imminent. “Why would they wait until after the elections here ... if they could initiate it and potentially gain the upper hand?” he said.Senior officers exit under HegsethSylvia's removal adds to a succession of departures among senior military leaders during Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth's tenure. He is the second general to leave the J5 director's post under Hegseth. Lt Gen Joseph McGee, his predecessor, was forced to retire last October.Before joining the Joint Staff, Sylvia commanded the 101st Airborne Division at Fort Campbell, Kentucky, until May 2025. He had previously served as vice director of the J5.The Joint Staff offered no explanation for the change but acknowledged Sylvia's service. “The Chairman, the Joint Staff, and the Joint Force extend our deepest gratitude to Lt Gen Brett Sylvia and his family for their 32 years of distinguished service to our nation,” a spokesperson said.Nearly two dozen generals, admirals and other military leaders have been fired, pressed to retire or otherwise departed under Hegseth, with the Pentagon publicly explaining few of the cases. The departures have included civilian leaders of the Army and Navy and senior uniformed officers across the services.Hegseth has also ordered a reduction in senior officer positions. Last month, he said the military should cut the number of top officers by 20% by January 1, 2027, doubling the planned reductions. The military has roughly 800 general and flag officer positions.“I call it accountability and long overdue,” Hegseth told junior officers and enlisted leaders at Marine Corps Base Quantico on September 30.The cuts have drawn criticism from some lawmakers, who argue that removing experienced commanders could damage military leadership over the longer term.“He's got some kind of like deep-seated grievance about leadership in the military,” Senator Mark Kelly, a former Navy combat pilot critical of Hegseth, said last month. “He's purging a generation of great leaders of the military, and it's going to take a generation to recover from it.”You use AI every day. articles.title: 68 killed in Spain train collision: Videos capture overturned carriages, injured passengers, devastation
articles.summary: At least 68 people have been killed and dozens injured after a high-speed train collision in Spain’s central province of Toledo.
articles.body: At least 68 people have been killed and dozens injured after a high-speed train collision in Spain’s central province of Toledo. Videos and photographs from the scene showed overturned carriages, injured passengers and emergency crews working to rescue people trapped in the wreckage.The collision occurred on Wednesday morning near Urda, about 120 km south of Madrid, on the Madrid-Seville rail route. Recordings captured by passengers showed scenes inside the trains following the impact, while images from the site showed carriages lying on their sides beside the tracks.Emergency services rushed to the scene to evacuate passengers, provide medical assistance and search the wreckage for survivors. Injured passengers were taken to nearby medical facilities, including a sports centre converted into a temporary treatment site. The regional government of Castilla-La Mancha said 58 people were receiving treatment in hospitals.According to Spain’s rail infrastructure operator ADIF, both trains were travelling south from Madrid towards Seville when the collision occurred. A state-owned RENFE train struck the rear of an IRYO train that had stopped on the tracks, derailing carriages on both trains.Spain’s transport minister Óscar Puente said a failure in the railway’s computer communications system had disrupted safety operations before the collision. The malfunction automatically stopped trains along a 63-kilometre stretch of track, after which the RENFE train was reportedly allowed to proceed despite a red signal.According to accounts of the incident, ADIF took manual control of the system following the failure. Puente said the train was authorised to continue under circumstances that investigators would need to examine.“There was a red signal prohibiting movement, yet the train was authorized to proceed,” Puente said at a press conference on Wednesday. “It is a decision made under inexplicable circumstances.”Meanwhile, Spanish trade union CSIF has demanded the resignation of the transport minister following the collision. The union accused Puente of shifting responsibility onto a railway official rather than accepting accountability for the disaster. Anger over the crash spilled onto the streets of Madrid on Wednesday night, when around 500 demonstrators gathered outside the Transport Ministry. Some protesters threw bottles and flares at police, prompting officers to deploy tear gas to disperse the crowd, Reuters reported.The RENFE train reportedly resumed its journey at about 124 miles per hour before hitting the stationary IRYO train. Authorities have yet to establish the full sequence of events leading to the crash.The disaster comes after another deadly rail collision in Spain earlier this year. A January crash in Córdoba province killed more than 40 people, while a separate incident near Barcelona claimed the life of a train driver.Rescue teams continued searching the damaged carriages as authorities worked to identify victims, assist survivors and establish the cause of the collision. Investigators are expected to examine the signalling system, communications failure and the decision to allow the train to proceed despite the red signal.You use AI every day. articles.title: US judge Alvin Hellerstein, who handled Maduro trial and Trump's hush money case, dies at 92
articles.summary: US federal judge Alvin K Hellerstein, who presided over cases involving Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro, President Donald Trump's hush money case and the
articles.body: US federal judge Alvin K Hellerstein, who presided over cases involving Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro, President Donald Trump's hush money case and the September 11 terror attacks.Hellerstein died on Wednesday morning surrounded by his family, Chief Judge Laura Taylor Swain said in a statement. He had served on the US District Court for the Southern District of New York since 1998 and continued hearing cases until his death.Swain described him as a “distinguished jurist”, praising his “energetic and dedicated service” to the court. “He is greatly appreciated and will be sorely missed,” she said, as quoted by AP.Hellerstein had continued to preside over Maduro's case despite questions about his age and health. Just two weeks before his death, he oversaw the arraignment of Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, on additional torture charges linked to their ongoing narco-terrorism conspiracy case.Maduro and Flores were captured during a US military raid in Caracas in January. When Maduro twice declined to enter a plea, Hellerstein directed that one be recorded on his behalf. “A plea of not guilty will be entered on behalf of Mr. Maduro,” he said.The judge had scheduled the trial for next June. Analisa Torres, a federal judge who previously served on the Manhattan state bench, will take over the case. She was also part of an international monitoring delegation for Venezuela's 2006 presidential election, won by Maduro's predecessor and mentor, Hugo Chávez.Maduro's lawyer, Barry Pollack, said, “We were saddened to learn of Judge Hellerstein’s passing and offer our condolences to his family.”Key cases handled by HellersteinHellerstein's nearly three decades on the federal bench brought him into contact with some of the most consequential legal disputes in the United States, from the aftermath of the 9/11 attacks to presidential immunity and international human rights cases.Trump's hush money conviction: In one of his final significant rulings, Hellerstein rejected Trump's attempt to move his New York hush money case to federal court and have the conviction dismissed on presidential immunity grounds. The case concerned a $130,000 payment to adult film actor Stormy Daniels before the 2016 election. “Paying hush money to an adult film star or engaging in a cover-up of an embarrassment are not subsumed in presidential immunity,” Hellerstein wrote in August.It was the third time he had rejected Trump's efforts to move the case to federal court. The ruling left Trump's conviction in place.September 11 lawsuits: Hellerstein oversaw civil litigation brought by victims and survivors of the September 11, 2001, attacks, including claims involving deaths, injuries and property damage. The cases continued for decades and became a defining part of his judicial career.In 2010, he had rejected a proposed settlement worth at least $575 million for thousands of people who had fallen ill after working amid toxic dust from the World Trade Center site. “This is different,” he said while explaining why he was intervening in the settlement process. “This is 9/11.”Lawyers said he spent hours meeting victims and their families and pushed back against settlement offers he considered inadequate.Trump and Michael Cohen: In 2020, Hellerstein ordered the release of Michael Cohen, Trump's former lawyer and fixer, from prison after the Justice Department revoked his home confinement. Cohen had argued that the move was intended to prevent him from publishing a book or speaking to the media. Hellerstein ruled that the government's action was retaliatory and violated Cohen's First Amendment rights.Sudan and BNP Paribas: In a 2025 civil case, Hellerstein presided over a trial in which a jury ordered French bank BNP Paribas to pay nearly $21 million to three Sudanese plaintiffs. The lawsuit alleged that the bank helped sustain the government of former Sudanese ruler Omar al-Bashir by providing access to the US financial system while atrocities were being committed.Abuse of detainees: In 2015, Hellerstein ordered the US government to release photographs documenting the abuse of detainees in Iraq and Afghanistan, another ruling that placed government accountability under scrutiny.His docket also included the criminal trials of Charlie Javice, convicted of defrauding JPMorgan Chase, and hedge fund founder Bill Hwang, convicted in 2024 of securities and market manipulation fraud.From military lawyer to federal judgeA New York native and Columbia Law School graduate, Hellerstein served in the US Army's Judge Advocate General's Corps from 1957 to 1960 before entering private legal practice in Manhattan.Then-president Bill Clinton nominated him to the federal bench in 1998. He assumed senior status in 2011 but continued to handle a substantial caseload.His rulings sometimes challenged the government and powerful institutions, including the Trump administration. articles.title: President Lyndon Johnson and Lady Bird Johnson created the garden in January 1969 for their grandchildren; more than 30 bronze handprints and footprints still mark the garden preserved on the White House grounds
articles.summary: Discover the hidden Children’s Garden at the White House, created by President Lyndon Johnson and Lady Bird Johnson in 1969 for their grandchildren. Explore the significance of the bronze handprints and footprints that tell the history of presidential families.
articles.body: There are some gardens located on the grounds of the White House and most of them are used for ceremonies or public purposes. People are familiar with the large lawns and the places where press conferences and photographs with floral decorations are taken. However, there is another, much smaller space which is located in the corner of the South Grounds and has a totally different purpose. It was created not for any ceremony, but for children. Presidential families often include young grandchildren, who visit the White House, which is a house, an office and a museum at the same time. The garden served as a secluded play area for presidential grandchildren, away from the bustle of the Executive Mansion. In addition, it became the source of the family history, as it has a physical mark of children who played there before.A garden created in January 1969, with two design creditsThe National Park Service says President Lyndon B. Johnson and his wife, Claudia Alta “Lady Bird” Johnson, created the Children’s Garden in January 1969. The agency credits the layout to Edward Durrell Stone and says it was scaled for young children. However, the White House Historical Association’s Texas and the White House website claims that the design is by Edward Durrell Stone Jr. and Edward Alexander. The White House Historical Association places the Children’s Garden on the South Lawn and dates its dedication to January 19, 1969, while the National Park Service says only that it was created in January 1969.Lady Bird Johnson’s diary entry of January 19, 1969Stewart D. McLaurin, President of the White House Historical Association, wrote Reflections: A Secret Garden, published on January 16, 2015, which quotes Lady Bird Johnson’s diary entry for January 19, 1969. In that entry, Lady Bird Johnson wrote, “Carrying an umbrella, I went down to the Children’s Garden, which will be our departing gift to the White House.” She saw the garden as a charming and very quiet place, even on a gray day. This is significant because the garden was completed during their last days in the house.The first commemorated grandchildrenThe first prints in the garden belonged to the Johnsons’ grandchildren, Patrick Lyndon Nugent and Lucinda Robb. Lucinda Robb Florio says hers were the first handprints left there, though she was far too young at the time to appreciate the White House. But the garden would certainly seem a suitable gift for someone who loved nature, like her grandmother.The same article includes recollections from Lauren Bush Lauren, a granddaughter of President George H. W. Bush, who was about five years old when she and her cousins made their handprints. The fresh blocks of cement were brought up to the Third Floor Solarium, making for a memorable and hectic day.19 grandchildren in 2015 against more than 30 castings todayThe two counts differ because they were published years apart and measure different things. The 2015 Historical Association article counts 19 presidential grandchildren who left prints in the garden during its first 45 years. The National Park Service now counts more than 30 castings, a figure that reflects later additions, including ten bronze handprint pavers for President Donald Trump’s ten grandchildren added in 2020, as Ivanka Trump announced and the fact that one child can have both a handprint and a footprint. The Texas and the White House website gives the garden’s size as 18 by 30 feet.The 2019 Tennis Pavilion review and the garden’s date of originThe National Capital Planning Commission June 2019 staff report titled"White House Grounds, Tennis Pavilion" mentions this garden being located west of the tennis courts. It is said that this garden serves as a private playground for the grandchildren of the President, which was established during the time of Lady Bird Johnson. This garden has footprints and handprints of the children and grandchildren of previous presidents embedded in the pavement. NCPC reports give its establishment as either 1968 or 1969, but the National Park Service dates its creation to January 1969 and the White House Historical Association dates its dedication to January 19, 1969. The later report in June 2019 mentioned that the next stage of the pavilion construction will involve moving the garden eastward. However, the NCPC's July 11, 2019 decision states that the tennis pavilion is the link between the garden and the tennis court.What the bronze prints recordThe Johnsons themselves made the garden, while successive presidential families later added bronze casts through their children. The association refers to the garden as a symbol of the relationship between the presidential families and the place where they used to live. Each cast represents one child on one day.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Pamela Anderson's garden at her childhood estate in Vancouver is a rustic vintage cottage straight out of a storybook: From embracing imperfection to consistency, gardening rules beginners can follow
articles.summary: While thinking of Pamela Anderson, a quiet vegetable patch may not be the first picture that comes to mind.
articles.body: While thinking of Pamela Anderson, a quiet vegetable patch may not be the first picture that comes to mind. Yet these days, the actor is just as happy with soil on her hands as she is under the spotlight.Back at her childhood home on Vancouver Island, Canada, she often takes to social media, posting pictures while she tends a gentle, cottage-style kitchen garden.She is quite active on Instagram and X and shares photos and videos of herself along with rows of raised beds, climbing squash, tall sunflowers, and fluffy pink roses. It looks like something out of a children's storybook. But what makes it special isn't a celebrity-sized budget. It is the calm, patient way she looks at growing things.In 2025, along with a garden tour, she collaborated with her skincare brand, Sonsie, to share seven simple rules she follows in the garden and in life that are short, simple, and easy to remember, which makes them perfect for anyone who has ever wanted to grow a few tomatoes but felt nervous about starting.What does Pamela Anderson’s vegetable and flower garden look likeSometime back, Pamela Anderson shared an Instagram video from her childhood home, and her kitchen garden caught the eye of her gardening fans for its relaxed, vintage cottage-style look.The garden has rows of raised wooden beds full of vegetables, herbs, and flowers that grow together, almost side by side. Willow obelisks and pretty trellises are taller plants adding length to the garden, and an archway covered in squash leads into the different growing areas. Tall sunflowers, soft pink roses, and a small tabletop greenhouse make the whole scene feel like a picture from a storybook.Whether you have a small garden in your backyard or pots installed in balcony, here are some gardening tips from Pamela's gardenPlant vegetables and flowers side by sideLavender grows beside onions, nasturtiums spill over the edges of the raised beds, and roses bloom among the vegetables. This combination and mix match, enhances the look of a vegetable patch, and it also attracts pollinators that help plants grow and produce well.ID@undefined Caption not available.ID@undefined Caption not available.ID@undefined Caption not available.Use raised beds and grow upwardsPamela's raised beds come in different sizes and heights, which gives the garden a layered, well-put look. Instead of straight formal rows, the changing levels add movement and make the space feel natural. She also makes smart use of vertical space for example, the squash-covered arch supports climbing crops, while willow obelisks and decorative trellises hold vines and flowering climbers.ID@undefined Caption not available.ID@undefined Caption not available.ID@undefined Caption not available.Don't hover, be gentle and stay consistentThree of Pamela's rules work together.First, no hovering, where Anderson advises giving plants what they need and leaving them be, "Hovering never helped anything grow." Second, handle everything with love, because plants remember how they are treated. Third, staying consistent, as gardens can't be rushed, and lasting results come from regular care rather than jsut shoprt term quick fixes.ID@undefined Caption not available.ID@undefined Caption not available.ID@undefined Caption not available.Forget perfection and let your garden grow its own wayPamela says, never to aim for perfection, and welcome the natural messiness of a garden. Look below the surface too, because strong roots are the real foundation of healthy plants. Let the garden evolve naturally instead of forcing everything into place, and celebrate differences rather than making everything uniform. As one of her Instagram posts say, "Life is like a garden… tend to it kindly, forgive the weeds, and cherish what blooms."You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.body: This month features relationships, personal choices, money, creativity, career moves, and shifting ambitions. Saturn in Pisces remains serious about partnerships, marriage, clients, and commitments. Venus will turn retrograde and enter Virgo on 6 November, Mercury will turn direct on 13 November, and the Rahu-Ketu shift on 25 November may begin to influence your approach to romance, creativity, children, friendships and long-term priorities.What to Do This MonthAhoi Ashtami falls on the same day as the Cancer Moon on 1 November, which focuses on gains, friendships, professional networks, and future ambitions. The Leo Moon on 3 November encourages private work, rest, expense management, and closure. Then the Moon in Virgo on 5 November puts your own needs and choices first. Venus goes retrograde in Virgo on 6 November, bringing Dhanteras and a need to reconsider what you want, who you want to be with, how you want to look, and what you previously decided.On 7 November, the Libra Moon is about personal values, family resources, savings and income. Narak Chaturdashi and Diwali fall on 8 November. The Scorpio Moon on 10 November is good for short journeys, business discussions, learning, paperwork and communication. Govardhan Puja also falls on this day. The end of Mercury’s combustion on 11 November may help with managing critical conversations in the long run.On the 12th, Mars moves into Leo and the Moon moves into Sagittarius. Energy may become more private, so it’s better to wait before investing time and resources in issues not ready for public action. Domestic duties, parents, property, and home are also activated.Mercury turns direct on 13 November, helping reorient plans that have been put on hold. On 15 November, the Capricorn Moon shines on personal projects, studies, romance, children and creativity. The Sun moves into Scorpio on 16 November, boosting practical decision-making and communication.On 17 November, the Aquarius Moon brings work, competition, health routines, and duties to the foreground. Starting 20 November, when the Moon enters Pisces, the emphasis shifts to partnerships, marriage, clients and agreements.On 22 November, Venus moves into Libra and the Moon moves into Aries. This energy shift will bring attention to income on one side and shared finances, debts, taxes, insurance, or trust on the other. When you talk about money, you may need to define what’s yours and what you handle jointly.On 24 November, the Taurus Moon favours travel, higher education, legal matters, mentors, and long-range thinking. On 25 November, Rahu moves into Capricorn, and Ketu moves into Cancer. This brings a major transformation in creativity, romance, children, speculation, friendships, and future aspirations.On 26 November, the Gemini Moon may give you more visibility in your career and stronger interactions with senior people. Cancer returns on 28 November, and the month ends with the Leo Moon on 30 November, encouraging private planning and recovery.What to AvoidDon’t let relationship uncertainty undermine your confidence in making decisions for your own life.Don’t gamble on a speculative possibility because Rahu makes it seem so exciting, romantic, or creative.Be cautious about spending more money to improve one’s social standing, comfort or appearance.Don’t assume every professional tie or friendship has to serve the same purpose in your future.How to Navigate This Month’s EnergySaturn in Pisces still tests Virgo in relationships and commitment. Stable relationships may shift toward more structured ones; uncertain relationships may require clearer expectations and firmer boundaries.Venus goes retrograde in Virgo on 6 November, bringing a particularly personal atmosphere to November. Old attractions, preferences, style choices, or unresolved emotional matters may resurface so you can evaluate whether they still fit the person you are becoming.The shift of Rahu-Ketu on 25 November brings yet another layer of change. Rahu in Capricorn can increase your creativity, romance, kids, study interests or calculated risk-taking. In Cancer, Ketu can slowly withdraw you from some social circles, group aspirations, or goals that no longer feel significant.Lucky AdvicePick something you are really excited about, but consider how long it will last. Stalin’s remarks came amid ongoing raids at the residence and properties of senior DMK functionary and former minister K N Nehru and his family members.He alleged that the raids were orchestrated merely to generate reels for the Tiruchy East bypoll and help Vijay deliver “theatrical punch dialogues on stage”. He declared that not even a primary member of the DMK would be intimidated by such actions.Asserting that the nation was mocking TVK’s governance over law and order failures, administrative stagnation and spiralling inflation, he said attempts to gag DMK leaders would fail.
